answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated escrowed trades with counterparties who already have established history; each completed trade releases a small bond, while disputes or detected collusion forfeit it. A newcomer can create a thousand identities, but those identities begin with no trusted counterparties, and circulating value among themselves does not build independent reputation. To gain reach, the attacker must fund bonds and persuade established agents to risk their own stake, tying up capital and exposing collaborators. An onyx, ember, or quill account gets no shortcut.
